Article Title: Two researchers may have just proved connected cars can be unlocked, started from thousands of miles away
Article Text:
Disclaimer: Its an AI-generated image used for representative purpose only

Inside the connected-car security flaws

In early 2026, two security researchers demonstrated that hackers could remotely unlock the doors and start the engines of internet-connected cars from anywhere in the world. Working together, white-hat hackers Shubham Shah and Sam Curry breached the backend connectivity systems of two major automakers. Beyond taking remote control of the vehicles, the flaws also exposed sensitive customer data, including personal information, vehicle locations, mileage, fuel levels, driving range, and whether the doors were locked or unlocked.In a note shared earlier this month, the duo said that both automakers have since patched the vulnerabilities, which stemmed from basic security oversights in the server APIs powering their mobile apps. Shah and Curry have not publicly named either company. However, they confirmed that the first automaker’s vulnerabilities affected vehicles in the US, while the second automaker’s flaws left cars open to remote unlocking across the US, Canada and Australia.While the researchers kept the brands anonymous, visual clues in their demonstration video, suggesting the second automaker may be Toyota, as per a report by Tom’s Hardware.According to the researchers’ write-ups, both companies relied on ForgeRock for user authentication and authorisation. Aside from one minor exception, the breaches weren't caused by ForgeRock itself but rather by how poorly the automakers implemented it. In a detailed breakdown of the second automaker’s Australian infrastructure, Shah explained how the duo gained access.After spending a couple of weeks studying how the automaker used ForgeRock, the researchers realised the easiest way was to generate their own access tokens for any user account. The pair used GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra to brute-force hidden URL paths. They eventually uncovered an unprotected endpoint that let them overwrite any user's password.The final hurdle was multi-factor authentication (MFA), which turned out to be misconfigured. In the Australian system, users could simply skip the MFA step altogether. By shuffling tokens between the mobile app and the backend endpoints, Shah and Curry were able to mint valid access tokens, fully impersonate any customer and send a "door-unlock" API request – promptly opening the test vehicle.
Article Summary: Security researchers demonstrated that hackers could remotely unlock the doors and start the engines of internet-connected cars from anywhere in the world. White-hat hackers Shubham Shah and Sam Curry breached the backend connectivity systems of two major automakers. The flaws also exposed sensitive customer data, including personal information, vehicle locations, mileage, fuel levels, driving range, and whether the doors were locked or unlocked.

Article Title: Days after donating $10 million to Nashville Symphony, Larry Ellison’s Oracle breaks ground on new 78-acre headquarters in Tennessee; aims to create thousands of high-quality jobs
Article Text:
Days after donating $10 million to Nashville Symphony, Larry Ellison’s Oracle breaks ground on new 78-acre headquarters in Tennessee; aims to create thousands of high-quality jobs

Oracle breaks ground on 70-acre Nashville headquarters

Oracle plans $175 million for public infrastructure

Oracle’s $10 million Nashville Symphony commitment

A month after committing $10 million to help keep the Nashville Symphony afloat during a financial crisis, Oracle has broken ground on its future global headquarters in Nashville, Tennessee. The November 11 ceremony marks another major step in the tech giant’s growing investment in the city, with plans for a sprawling riverfront campus expected to create thousands of high-quality jobs. The development, it said, will strengthen Oracle’s presence in a city increasingly positioning itself as a hub for technology and healthcare, while also bringing new public infrastructure, green spaces, retail and hospitality facilities to Nashville’s East Bank.Oracle CEOs Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia joined Tennessee Governor Bill Lee, Nashville Mayor Freddie O’Connell, Governor-elect Marsha Blackburn and other state and local leaders for the groundbreaking ceremony. The planned campus will span approximately 78 acres in Nashville’s East Bank, transforming a former industrial site into a new headquarters for Oracle’s growing cloud, AI and healthcare technology operations.The first buildings are expected to open in 2030. The development will include retail spaces, a 120-room Nobu hotel and restaurant, and more than 1,900 trees. Oracle is also targeting LEED Gold certification across the campus.The company said it has already recruited engineering and technical talent locally and expects hiring to accelerate over the coming years. Its Nashville workforce includes healthcare technology professionals, as well as teams in sales, marketing and other business functions.Beyond the headquarters, Oracle’s investment includes $175 million for public infrastructure improvements. These include a pedestrian bridge across the Cumberland River, a public park, greenway connections and street upgrades.The planned bridge is expected to connect surrounding neighbourhoods with the campus and park, providing new routes for everyday travel and recreation. Nashville Mayor Freddie O’Connell said the development would help make the East Bank more accessible to residents.“Our East Bank should bring us closer together as Nashvillians, serving as a guide for how we build great communities,” said O’Connell.Oracle’s growing investment in Nashville also includes support for local cultural institutions.On October 4, the company announced a $10 million partnership with the Nashville Symphony as the organisation faced a financial emergency. The funding helped the Symphony reinstate its 2026-27 season and bring back full-time staff and orchestra members who were scheduled to be furloughed on October 18.Oracle CEO Clay Magouyrk said the company wanted to help address community needs as it builds its headquarters in the city.“Nashville is a city that understands how music can bring people together,” Magouyrk said. “We are part of this community and understand how important cultural institutions like this are to the residents of Nashville. As Oracle builds its new headquarters on Nashville’s East Bank, we are here to help solve the community’s problems and ensure Nashville remains a vibrant place to live and work for generations to come. ”Oracle has also announced a $1.55 million grant to Trinity Community Commons for renovations to its community hub and dining room, alongside $150,000 in grants to 30 local nonprofits through its employee-directed giving programme.
Article Summary: Oracle breaks ground on new 78-acre headquarters in Tennessee. Plans for a sprawling riverfront campus expected to create thousands of high-quality jobs. The development will include retail spaces, a 120-room Nobu hotel and restaurant, and more than 1,900 trees.

Article Title: Colette Kress, Ian Buck and five others who could be Nvidia’s next CEO as the company prepares to fire Jensen Huang
Article Text:
Who replaces Jensen Huang?

Nvidia’s flat structure left no obvious successor to Jensen Huang

Colette Kress is the safest pair of hands for the interim job

Ian Buck has the strongest claim among the engineers

Rene Haas is the outsider who already knows the culture

Johny Srouji would bring Apple's chip discipline

Eric Schmidt is the caretaker some would reach for

Madison Huang is the family name with the most visible rise

Nico Caprez, Huang’s son-in-law, has become the family's power broker

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia's most likely move is Kress now and a longer search after

Nvidia has never had to think seriously about who comes after Jensen Huang. He co-founded the company in 1993, has been its only chief executive since, and built it so completely around himself that succession always felt like a question for some distant year. That year may have arrived this week.On November 8, the chipmaker's board opened an independent investigation following reports that Huang, 63, had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The New York Times had reported on October 29 that Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed, sought to cultivate close ties with him, and both the Times and the Financial Times reported that US intelligence agencies suspect she was passing information to Beijing. In an email to staff on November 8, Huang admitted to the affair. China has dismissed the allegations as a smear. The board said it still had confidence in him, and on November 10 it hired Joon H. Kim, a former acting US attorney for the Southern District of New York, at law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead the probe.By November 11, the mood had turned. The New York Times reported that Huang had also been in a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare and one of his direct reports.Minutes later, The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to force him out. Directors met late into the night, shares fell more than 9% in after-hours trading, and Bloomberg reported that the board is working with an outside firm to explore replacements. At the time of writing, the company has not announced a decision.Under the company's bylaws, a majority of directors can replace the CEO without cause. The harder part is finding the name that goes in his place.Jensen Huang runs one of the flattest structures in big tech. He had 55 direct reports in 2024 and 36 by late 2025, and he skips one-on-one meetings so that every leader hears the same thing at the same time. Asked about succession, he has said there will "never be one like me," while arguing that the dozens of executives around him could each run a company of their own because they have watched him make every decision.That design kept Nvidia fast. It also means nobody below Huang has ever held a view of the whole company. The bench got thinner in August, when Jay Puri, who ran worldwide sales for two decades, retired and handed over to former Microsoft executive Nick Parker.These are the seven names now in the frame, two of them from Huang's own family.Kress has been chief financial officer since 2013. Before that she was CFO of Cisco's business technology and operations finance organisation, and spent 13 years at Microsoft, the last four as CFO of its Server and Tools division, after starting out in finance at Texas Instruments. After Huang, she is the executive investors know best, the voice that has walked Wall Street through every quarter of the AI boom, including a fiscal 2026 in which revenue grew 65% to $215.9 billion. Semafor reported that some directors favour naming her interim CEO.The doubt is about what comes after. Her entire career has been in finance, and analysts do not see her as a natural successor to Huang's role as the company's technology visionary. As a stabiliser while the board searches, though, no one else is as ready. She already owns the numbers the market is holding the company to, including her own forecast of 70% revenue growth in fiscal 2028.Buck created CUDA, the software platform that made Nvidia's GPUs the default choice for AI work and that rivals still struggle to match. The idea began at Stanford, where his PhD work produced Brook, an early attempt at running general-purpose code on graphics chips, and Nvidia hired him in 2004 to turn it into a product. In roughly 22 years at the company, he has risen to run hyperscale and high-performance computing, the heart of the data centre business that now brings in most of its revenue. His job puts him in daily contact with Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta and OpenAI.Bettors on Polymarket have him as favourite for the permanent role. He also brings something this moment needs, having testified before the US Congress on AI and advised the White House. Some analysts have floated a shared interim arrangement, with Kress handling the finances and Buck the technology and customer relationships. The open question is whether a product leader who has never run the whole company can carry its public face the way Huang did.Haas has been CEO of Arm since 2022, but before that he spent seven years at Nvidia, rising to run its computing products business. He took Arm public in 2023, and in March he moved it beyond licensing designs to selling its own chip for the first time, a data centre processor called the AGI CPU, with Meta as its first customer. Few outsiders combine first-hand knowledge of how Huang operates with experience steering a listed chip company through that kind of change.Futurum Group analyst Shay Boloor wrote on X that if he had to bet on an external pick, it would be Haas. Polymarket odds on him have since dropped sharply, and the timing works against him. Having just put Arm into competition with some of its own customers, Nvidia among them, he would be walking away from the biggest bet of his tenure.Srouji led Apple's in-house silicon programme from its first chip, the A4, in 2008, through to the processors that now power every iPhone and Mac, and his group went on to take over batteries, cameras, displays and Apple's own cellular modems. Before Apple, he worked on processor design at Intel and IBM. In April, Apple made him chief hardware officer, placing its entire hardware engineering organisation under him as John Ternus prepared to take over from Tim Cook.His name has come up as a possible external successor. On paper, he offers what Kress cannot: an engineer who built a chip team from scratch inside a company that had never designed its own processors. The difficulty is timing. He has only just been handed the largest role of his career in Cupertino, which would make him hard to lure away.The former Google CEO is the least conventional name here, and he already has a job: since March 2025 he has been CEO and controlling shareholder of rocket maker Relativity Space. Still, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of the Yale School of Management, who advises chief executives and boards, has said he has heard Schmidt rumoured as a possible choice and that Schmidt "could step in tomorrow and do a very good job."Schmidt ran Google from 2001 to 2011, taking it from a fast-growing search company to a global giant, and has since spent years on AI and national security policy in Washington. That last part matters now. A board dealing with a spy investigation, congressional pressure and nervous shareholders may value a calm, well-connected figure more than an engineer, at least for a while.Jensen Huang's daughter took a route into technology unlike anyone else on this list. She trained at The Culinary Institute of America and Le Cordon Bleu, cooked in restaurant kitchens, then spent close to four years at LVMH marketing champagne brands such as Dom Pérignon and Veuve Clicquot. In 2019 she started an MBA at London Business School and took a short AI course at MIT, and in 2020 she joined Nvidia as a marketing intern. She is now senior director of product and technical marketing for the company's physical AI platforms, including Omniverse, Cosmos and Isaac.Her growing number of public appearances with her father, including at the World Robot Conference in Beijing in August, has fed talk that she is being prepared for more, and former employees have said her influence reaches beyond her formal marketing role. Still, Nvidia's 2026 proxy filing shows she is not an executive officer and does not report directly to her father. Huang has said his children would have to earn the top job, and a jump from senior director to CEO would be a hard sell to shareholders already rattled by this week.Caprez, 35, is a former Swiss national team ski racer who studied banking and finance at the University of Zurich and worked as a consultant at BCG before meeting Madison as a classmate at London Business School. He joined Nvidia in early 2024 as a corporate development manager, recruited with her help, and became vice president of global AI infrastructure growth in January. The two married in Hawaii in September.The Information, which spoke to more than a dozen people who work with him, described Caprez as Huang's "consigliere" and the company's main contact for neoclouds, the newer cloud providers that rent out Nvidia GPUs. Brookfield's Sikander Rashid has recalled Huang telling him that if he wanted something done, he should talk to Nico. One colleague told the publication they imagined Huang was preparing Madison and Caprez for the next step. Less than three years at the company, though, would make his case harder to defend than anyone else's here.Patrick Moorhead of Moor Insights & Strategy has compared the moment to Intel's 2018 removal of Brian Krzanich over a relationship with an employee, while noting that the chip plans are set years ahead, so the near-term risk to the business is limited. D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria was blunter, warning that the episode could force a transition the company is not prepared for. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney went the other way, saying that removing Huang would be as foolish as Apple's firing of Steve Jobs.If the board does move, the first name announced is most likely to be Kress. Reports that directors favour her as interim CEO, her 13 years as the company's public financial voice and the board's need to steady investors all point the same way. The permanent job will take a longer search, and on current signals Buck is the insider best placed for it, possibly after a spell sharing the interim role with Kress. Huang always argued that Nvidia did not need a formal succession plan because everyone around him had seen how he thinks. The board is about to find out whether he was right.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993, has been its only chief executive since. Colette Kress is the safest pair of hands for the interim job. Ian Buck has the strongest claim among the engineers. Rene Haas is the outsider who already knows the culture. Johny Srouji would bring Apple's chip discipline. Eric Schmidt is the caretaker some would reach for.

What should Google Chrome users do

The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued a warning for Google Chrome, asking users to update their browser immediately. In an advisory rated ‘critical’, the cyber agency said multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in Google Chrome which could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code, bypass security restrictions, or cause denial of service (Dos) conditions on the targeted system. The versions impacted by these vulnerabilities include Google Chrome versions prior to 157.0.8103.50 and Google Chrome Extended Stable versions prior to 156.0.8078.96.In the advisory, the CERT-In says that all Google Chrome users are at high “risk of arbitrary code execution and compromise of affected systems”.“These vulnerabilities exist in Google Chrome due to use after free in XML, type confusion in V8, out-of-bounds write in GPU, incorrect authorization in FileSystem, buffer overflow in Compositing, and uninitialized resource bugs in WebGL and GPU,” the agency said.CERT-In says that the vulnerability in Google Chrome can allow a remote attacker to persuade a victim to visit a specially crafted webpage. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code, bypass security restrictions, or cause denial of service (DoS) conditions on the targeted system.“This vulnerability (CVE-2026-125350) is being actively exploited in the wild.Users are strongly advised to apply the latest patches immediately,” the agency said.Google Chrome users are advised to apply appropriate updates. Google has released a stable channel update for desktop users. Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild, the tech giant said adding “The Stable channel has been updated to 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and Mac and 157.0.8103.50 to Linux which will roll out over the coming days/weeks”.
Article Summary: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has issued a warning for Google Chrome, asking users to update their browser immediately. In an advisory rated ‘critical’, the cyber agency said multiple vulnerabilities have been reported in Google Chrome which could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code, bypass security restrictions, or cause denial of service conditions.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos' father fled Cuba with 3 shirts at 16; 33 years later, he and his wife invested $250,000 of their savings in Amazon, a bet that could now be worth more than the GDP of 100 countries
Article Text:
Image: Getty Images

Jeff Bezos’ father fled Cuba as a teenager under Operation Pedro Pan

From a refugee camp to a career at Exxon

How Jeff Bezos' parents invested nearly $250,000 in Amazon

Amazon's growth transformed the value of its early shares

The value of the Bezos family's Amazon investment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Miguel and Jackie Bezos' philanthropic work

At 16, Miguel Bezos left Cuba for the United States with just three shirts, three pairs of trousers, a pair of shoes and a handmade jacket. Arriving as an unaccompanied teenager during a period of political upheaval in Cuba, he had to rebuild his life in a country where he did not even speak the language. Over the next three decades, he completed his education, established a career in engineering and management, and started a family. In 1995, 33 years after leaving Cuba, he and his wife, Jackie Bezos, invested nearly $250,000 of their hard-earned savings in their son Jeff Bezos ' fledgling online bookstore, Amazon, despite being warned that they could lose the entire amount. That early investment, based on subsequent stock splits and assuming the original shares were retained, could be worth more than $90 billion today, exceeding the annual GDP of more than 100 countries.Born in Santiago de Cuba, Miguel Bezos left his home country in 1962 as part of Operation Pedro Pan, a programme that enabled thousands of Cuban children to travel to the United States without their parents. The migration took place amid concerns among Cuban families about the political changes following Fidel Castro's rise to power. Many parents believed sending their children to America would give them access to better opportunities and a safer future.Miguel arrived in Miami on July 21, 1962, at the age of 16. According to an account published by Amazon, he carried three shirts, three pairs of trousers, a pair of shoes and a handmade jacket. His mother had made the jacket using cleaning cloths because the family had limited resources.He initially stayed at Camp Matecumbe, a refugee centre in Florida, before being transferred to a Catholic institution in Wilmington, Delaware. His parents expected their separation to be temporary, but Miguel had to begin adapting to an unfamiliar country, a different culture and a language he did not know.Miguel continued his education in the United States, attending Salesianum School in Wilmington, Delaware. He later received a scholarship to the University of Albuquerque in New Mexico, where he studied mathematics and graduated in 1968.During his university years, he met Jacklyn Gise, known as Jackie. The couple married in 1968. Jackie already had a son, Jeff Bezos, from her previous marriage. Miguel adopted Jeff when he was four years old, becoming his father and helping raise him.After graduating, Miguel built a professional career in engineering and management at Exxon. He worked for the energy company for more than three decades, taking up positions that provided financial stability for his family. His experience as an immigrant who had rebuilt his life through education and professional work would later form an important part of the Bezos family's story.In 1994, Jeff Bezos decided to leave his job at investment firm D E Shaw and pursue an opportunity he saw in the rapidly expanding internet. He moved to establish an online bookstore, which would eventually become Amazon.His parents became among his earliest financial backers. In February 1995, Miguel personally invested $100,000 in the company. A separate investment of $145,500 followed in July 1995 through Jackie's family trust. Together, their contributions amounted to approximately $245,500, commonly rounded to $250,000.The decision involved a considerable financial risk. Jeff later recalled warning his parents that there was a 70% chance they could lose their entire investment. He also remembered that his father initially asked him what the internet was, as the technology was still unfamiliar to many people at the time.Despite the uncertainty, Miguel and Jackie decided to support their son. Jeff later explained that his parents were investing in him rather than simply betting on the idea of an online bookstore. Their decision came at a time when Amazon was still a small start-up with no guarantee of becoming a successful business.Amazon launched its online bookstore in July 1995, initially selling books to customers through its website. The business expanded rapidly, receiving orders from all 50 US states and 45 countries within its first 30 days.The company went public in May 1997 at $18 per share, raising approximately $54 million. Over the following years, Amazon expanded beyond books into electronics, clothing, cloud computing, entertainment and other services, becoming one of the world's largest technology companies.Its growth also increased the potential value of shares acquired by its earliest investors. Amazon carried out four stock splits: a 2-for-1 split in 1998, two additional splits in 1999, and a 20-for-1 split in 2022. Together, these increased the original share count 240 times.The stock splits meant that early shareholders who retained their holdings would own substantially more shares than they originally purchased, although the value of each individual share adjusted accordingly.Based on the original share purchases and the cumulative effect of Amazon's stock splits, the combined parental investment of approximately $245,500 could theoretically represent around 343.3 million shares.Using an illustrative Amazon closing price of $266.93 on November 9, 2026, the original combined shareholding would have a hypothetical value of approximately $91.63 billion, assuming all the original shares had been retained.The figure offers a striking comparison with the annual economic output of entire countries. According to World Bank data, Panama's nominal gross domestic product was approximately $90.46 billion in 2025. The hypothetical value of the original investment would therefore be slightly higher than Panama's annual GDP.At that valuation, the investment would also exceed the annual GDP of more than 100 countries and economies, depending on the GDP dataset and year used. The comparison illustrates the scale of Amazon's growth from a small online bookstore into a global technology business.Beyond their involvement in Amazon's early years, Miguel and Jackie Bezos also established a philanthropic presence through the Bezos Family Foundation, which they co-founded in 2000. The foundation supports initiatives focused on education, child development and opportunities for young people.The family has also donated substantial Amazon holdings over the years. Reports have documented transfers of Amazon shares to the foundation between 2001 and 2016, reflecting the couple's involvement in philanthropic activities as the company grew.Miguel's journey from an unaccompanied Cuban teenager arriving in America with a few belongings to an engineer, father and early Amazon investor has remained an important part of the history behind the company.
Article Summary: Miguel and Jackie Bezos invested $250,000 in their son's online bookstore, Amazon, despite being warned they could lose the entire amount. That early investment, based on subsequent stock splits and assuming the original shares were retained, could be worth more than $90 billion today, exceeding the annual GDP of more than 100 countries.
